title: refusals: one throw answers one declared sentence — an action that refuses a selection for several reasons at once cannot list them in the person's language (after #34273)
body:
## What

Since #34273 a `type: 'script'` action can declare a `refusals` catalogue, and the server answers a refusal in the request's `Accept-Language`. That works — but **one throw answers exactly one declared sentence**: one `code`, at most one `reason`, one flat `params` object.

An action that checks a whole selection and refuses all-or-nothing has several things to say at once — one sentence per offending record, each with its own reason and its own values. That answer cannot be expressed through the catalogue, so such an action has to choose between a list in the author's language and a single reason in the person's language.

The resolver is shared with hooks (`resolveSandboxedRefusal`), so a hook that wants to name several reasons in one refusal meets the same limit. Only the action side was measured.

## Where we hit it

HotCRM 6.6.0, `crm_expense.submit_for_reimbursement` and `submit_trip_for_reimbursement` (one shared script body). A person selects expenses and submits them; when some cannot go, nothing is submitted and the answer lists why, today as English literals:

```
Expense Taxi 12 is already on an expense report.
Expense Hotel 7 is already approved.
Travel request TR-00001 is not approved yet. Only an approved travel request can be reported against.
2 selected expenses are not yours, or no longer exist.
Nothing was submitted.
```

In a zh-CN console the person reads this in English (objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2759). Moving it into `refusals` is not possible without either dropping the list or leaving it untranslated.

## Measured on 18.6.0

Booted stack through `@objectstack/verify`, `POST /api/v1/actions/crm_expense/submit_for_reimbursement`, once with `accept-language: en` and once with `zh-CN`. Probe catalogue on the action, with zh-CN rows under `objects.crm_expense._actions.submit_for_reimbursement.refusals.…`:

```ts
refusals: {
  PROBE_PLAIN: { message: 'Probe plain sentence.' },
  PROBE: {
    message: 'Probe entry {{ name }} x{{ count }}.',
    status: 409,
    params: ['name', 'count'],
    reasons: {
      on_report: { message: 'Expense {{ name }} is already on an expense report ({{ count | number }}).' },
      approved: { message: 'Expense {{ name }} is already approved.' },
    },
  },
},
```

| The body throws an `Error` carrying | Answer |
|---|---|
| `{ code: 'PROBE_PLAIN' }` | 400, `declaredCode: PROBE_PLAIN`; `Probe plain sentence.` / `探针：普通句子。` — works |
| `{ code: 'PROBE', reason: 'on_report', params: { name: 'Taxi 12', count: 3 } }` | 409; `Expense Taxi 12 is already on an expense report (3).` / `费用 Taxi 12 已在报销单上（3）。` — works |
| `params.name = ['Taxi 12', 'Hotel 7']` | the array is rendered as JSON: `Expense ["Taxi 12","Hotel 7"] is already on an expense report (2).` |
| `reason: ['on_report', 'approved']` | ignored — the entry sentence, once |
| `reasons: [ … ]` | ignored — the entry sentence, once |
| `refusals: [ { code, reason, params }, … ]` | ignored — the entry sentence with empty holes: `Probe entry  x.` |
| `params: [ { … }, { … } ]` | ignored — holes empty |
| an undeclared reason or code (computed at run), no code with its own `userMessage`, a plain `Error`, an `AggregateError` | 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| a declared code plus its own `userMessage` and `status` | both ignored; the catalogue sentence and status answer |

In source (`@objectstack/runtime` `readRefusalAddress` / `declaredAnswer`): the address read off the error is `reason` only when it is a non-empty string and `params` only when it is a non-array object. The `template` dialect's formatters (`upper lower trim number currency percent date datetime truncate default json`) have no list or repeat construct, so "one line per record" cannot be written inside one declared sentence either.

## Expected

One refusal can name several declared reasons, each with its own params, and the answer carries each one's sentence in the person's language, in the order thrown. For example a throw carrying, under one declared code, an ordered list of `{ reason, params }` — every reason checked against the catalogue as a single reason is today (refused at save when written literally, a fault at run otherwise), each rendered from its translated sentence, the entry's own `message` available as the closing line (`Nothing was submitted.`). How the list is shaped on the wire and in the console is yours to rule; the app only needs each declared sentence to arrive translated.

A list formatter in the template would cover the simplest case (the same sentence over several names) but not this one, where the lines have different reasons.

## Workaround

None that keeps the rule that no hook or action composes language itself. Once `refusals` is declared, text outside the catalogue never reaches the person (the rows above), which is the right contract — and the reason the app cannot bridge this. Pre-rendering the lines into a string param leaves the list in the author's language inside a translated frame; refusing on the first problem alone drops the list the person relies on. HotCRM leaves these sentences in English and waits: objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2759 is blocked by this card.
